Do Reasonable Alternative Analyses Agree?

Source: R/evidence.R
cpsspec.Rd

Runs several specifications of the same estimate (other covariates, another model, another handling of outliers or missing values) and reports how far they spread and whether they agree in sign. A finding that holds under one specification only is fragile; one that survives the reasonable alternatives is robust.

Usage

cpsspec(data, specs)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

specs

A named list of functions, each taking the data frame and returning one number: the estimate under that specification. The first is the one the paper reports.

Value

A list of class rmbl_spec: ok (every estimate has the sign of the reported one), table (spec, estimate, same_sign), reported, range and share (the share agreeing in sign). It prints as a box and goes into a manifest with recevid().

See also

cpsplant(), recevid().

Examples

set.seed(2)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(300), z = rnorm(300))
d$y <- 0.5 * d$x + 0.3 * d$z + rnorm(300)
cpsspec(d, list(
  adjusted = function(df) coef(lm(y ~ x + z, df))[["x"]],
  simple = function(df) coef(lm(y ~ x, df))[["x"]],
  trimmed = function(df) {
    keep <- abs(df$y - mean(df$y)) < 3 * sd(df$y)
    coef(lm(y ~ x + z, df[keep, ]))[["x"]]
  }
))
#> ╭── Specification check: robust ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │ ✔ VERIFIED                                                                  │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Specifications         3                                                  │
#> │   Reported               0.574115 (adjusted)                                │
#> │   Range                  0.56001 to 0.574115                                │
#> │   Same sign as reported  3 of 3                                             │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   specification  estimate  sign                                             │
#> │   -------------  --------  ----                                             │
#> │   adjusted         0.5741  same                                             │
#> │   simple           0.5603  same                                             │
#> │   trimmed          0.5600  same                                             │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Every specification agrees in sign with the reported one, so the finding  │
#> │   does not hang on one analytic choice.                                     │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
